summary: Someone bought an animal from a non-Jew and does not know if it gave birth before. Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva argue how we decide if its next male baby is a bechor.

chunks.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מִן הַנָּכְרִי וְאֵין יָדוּעַ
chunks.en: Someone who buys an animal from a non-Jew and does not know
chunks.st: In the case of one who purchases a female animal from a gentile and does not know

chunks.en: whether it gave birth before or did not give birth before:
chunks.st: whether it had previously given birth or whether it had not previously given birth,
chunks.stMore: and after the purchase the animal gave birth to a male,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says: If the mother was

chunks.en: if it is a goat in its first year, the baby surely goes to the Kohen;
chunks.st: a goat within its first year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest, as it definitely never gave birth previously.

chunks.en: if it is older, it is a doubt.
chunks.st: From that point forward, i.e., if the mother is older than that, its offspring’s status as a firstborn is uncertain.

chunks.en: If it is a sheep in its second year, the baby surely goes to the Kohen;
chunks.st: If it was a ewe within its second year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest;

chunks.en: if it is older, it is a doubt.
chunks.st: from that point forward an offspring’s status is uncertain.

chunks.he: פָּרָה וַחֲמוֹר בְּנוֹת שָׁלשׁ וַדַּאי לַכֹּהֵן,
chunks.en: If it is a cow or a donkey in its third year, the baby surely goes to the Kohen;
chunks.st: If it was a cow or a donkey within its third year the male offspring certainly is given to the priest;

chunks.en: if it is older, it is a doubt.
chunks.st: from that point forward the offspring’s status is uncertain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: If an animal became free from the bechor only by having a baby,
chunks.st: Were an animal exempted only by giving birth to an offspring and in no other manner the halakha would be

chunks.en: it would be as you say.
chunks.st: in accordance with your statement.

chunks.en: But the Sages said
chunks.st: But the Sages said:

chunks.en: that a small animal can show other signs that it was going to have a baby,
chunks.st: An indication of the offspring in a small animal is a murky discharge
chunks.stMore: from the womb, which indicates the animal had been pregnant, and therefore exempts subsequent births from the mitzva of the firstborn.

chunks.en: and a big animal too,
chunks.st: The indication in a large animal is the emergence of an afterbirth,

chunks.en: and so can a woman.
chunks.st: and the indication in a woman is a fetal sac or an afterbirth.
chunks.stMore: Since these can be produced even within a year, it cannot be assumed that an animal in its first year is definitely subject to the mitzva of the firstborn. Rabbi Akiva continues:

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: Rather, this is the principle:

chunks.en: Any animal that we know gave birth before,
chunks.st: In any case where it is known that the animal had previously given birth,

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest has nothing here.

chunks.en: And any animal that did not give birth before,
chunks.st: And in any case where it is known that the animal had not previously given birth,

chunks.en: this goes to the Kohen.
chunks.st: that is given to the priest.

chunks.en: If it is a doubt,
chunks.st: And if it is uncertain,

chunks.en: the owners eat it once it gets a blemish.
chunks.st: it may be eaten in its blemished state by the owner.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: In the case of

chunks.en: a big animal that gave out a lump of blood
chunks.st: a large animal that expelled a mass of congealed blood,

chunks.en: must bury it,
chunks.st: that mass must be buried.
chunks.stMore: The reason is that perhaps there was a male fetus there which was consecrated as a firstborn when it emerged,

chunks.en: and the animal is now free from the bechor.
chunks.st: and the animal is exempt from having any future offspring counted a firstborn.

summary: Someone who buys a nursing animal, or sees his animals nursing babies, may assume each one is nursing its own baby.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: someone who buys a nursing animal from a non-Jew
chunks.st: In the case of one who purchases a nursing female animal from a gentile,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא בְנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת הָיָה.
chunks.en: does not worry that maybe it was nursing another animal's baby.
chunks.st: he does not need to be concerned, i.e., take into account the possibility, that perhaps it was nursing the offspring of another
chunks.stMore: animal. Rather, the buyer may assume it had previously given birth. In the case of one who

chunks.en: If he went into his flock
chunks.st: enters amid his flock

chunks.en: and saw the first-time mothers nursing,
chunks.st: and sees mother animals that gave birth for the first time that were nursing,

chunks.en: and the mothers that were not first-time also nursing,
chunks.st: and also sees mother animals that gave birth not for the first time that were also nursing,

chunks.en: he does not worry
chunks.st: he does not need to be concerned

chunks.en: that maybe the baby of this one
chunks.st: that perhaps the offspring of this animal

chunks.en: went over to that one,
chunks.st: came to that animal to be nursed,

chunks.en: or that maybe the baby of that one
chunks.st: or that perhaps the offspring of that animal

chunks.en: went over to this one.
chunks.st: came to this animal to be nursed.

summary: The Torah forbids shearing a bechor. So when shechting it, or checking its blemish, a person may only pull out a little wool and must leave it in place.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
chunks.stMore: Since it is prohibited by Torah law to shear a firstborn, as it states: “And you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock” (Deuteronomy 15:19),

chunks.en: someone who shechts a bechor
chunks.st: one who is slaughtering a firstborn,
chunks.stMore: and must clear hair or wool from the area of the neck in order to facilitate proper slaughter,

chunks.en: makes room on its neck with a cleaver, here and there,
chunks.st: clears space by uprooting the hair with a cleaver [bekofitz] from here and from there, on either side of the neck,

chunks.en: and pulls out the wool,
chunks.st: although he thereby plucks out the hair. He may clear space in this manner

chunks.en: as long as he does not move it from its place.
chunks.st: provided that he does not move the plucked hair from its place;
chunks.stMore: it must remain intermingled with the rest of the hair so it will appear that he did not shear the animal.

chunks.en: The same is true for someone who pulls out wool
chunks.st: And likewise, one plucks the hair to enable one of the Sages

chunks.en: to see the place of the blemish.
chunks.st: to examine the place of a blemish
chunks.stMore: and thereby determine whether it is permitted to slaughter the firstborn outside the Temple.

summary: Wool that fell off a bechor with a blemish: the Rabbis argue whether it may be used. The mishnah also teaches about wool hanging loose from a bechor.

chunks.en: The wool of a bechor with a blemish that fell out,
chunks.st: With regard to the hair of a blemished firstborn animal that shed from the animal,

chunks.en: and he put it in a window shelf, and later he shechted the bechor:
chunks.st: and which one placed in a compartment for safekeeping, and thereafter he slaughtered
chunks.stMore: the animal; given that after the animal dies he is permitted to derive benefit from the hair the animal had on its body when it died, what is the halakhic status of hair that shed from the animal while it was alive?

chunks.en: Akavya ben Mahalalel allows it,
chunks.st: Akavya ben Mahalalel deems its use permitted,

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem its use prohibited; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

chunks.en: Akavya did not allow this case.
chunks.st: It was not with regard to that case that Akavya ben Mahalalel deemed use of the wool permitted.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא בִשְׂעַר בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁנָּשַׁר
chunks.en: Rather, it was the wool of a bechor with a blemish that fell out,
chunks.st: Rather, it was in the case of the hair of a blemished firstborn animal that shed from the animal

chunks.en: and he put it in a window shelf, and later the bechor died.
chunks.st: which one placed in a compartment and thereafter the animal died.

chunks.en: In this case Akavya ben Mahalalel allows it,
chunks.st: It was in that case that Akavya ben Mahalalel deems use of the wool permitted,

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem its use prohibited even after its death.

chunks.en: Wool that hangs loose on a bechor:
chunks.st: With regard to wool that is dangling from a firstborn animal, i.e., which was not completely shed,

chunks.he: אֶת שֶׁהוּא נִרְאֶה מִן הַגִּזָּה, מֻתָּר.
chunks.en: the part that looks like part of the fleece is allowed,
chunks.st: that which appears to be part of the fleece is permitted when the animal is shorn after its death,

chunks.he: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה מִן הַגִּזָּה, אָסוּר:
chunks.en: and the part that does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.
chunks.st: and that which does not appear to be part of the fleece is prohibited.
